title: Canonical source, derived artifacts and mutable state stay separate
summary: Every write path in the deployment is classified as canonical source, reproducible derived artifact, or mutable runtime state; backup, retention, evidence and edit rules follow the class.

protected.asset: Recoverability and evidentiary value of every document and artifact the deployment produces
protected.failure: A derived artifact is treated as irreplaceable source, or mutable runtime state is edited as if it were canonical, so losses and divergence become undetectable.

rationale: Recovery, review and privacy decisions all depend on knowing which copy is authoritative. Canonical sources change only under review and keep history; derived artifacts are reproducible from recorded inputs and are disposable; mutable runtime state is expected to change and is never cited as evidence. Mixing the classes makes a cache deletion look like data loss, makes a hand-edited runtime file look like a reviewed decision, and lets two stores both claim to be the canonical copy of the same record.

variants.description: Each write path is assigned exactly one class; backup, retention and evidence rules follow the class label.
Derived artifacts record the digest of their exact inputs and generator version, so they can be reproduced byte-identically or invalidated when inputs change.

verification.method: List the deployment's write paths, confirm each carries exactly one class label, and reproduce one derived artifact from its recorded inputs byte-identically.
verification.evidence: The classification list plus the digest comparison of the reproduced artifact against the original; no content of the stores.

rollback.method: Reclassify the mislabelled store; classification is metadata and moves no data.
rollback.safety: Reclassification never deletes the old copy until its class is confirmed by reproduction or backup.

failure_modes: A derived report is backed up while its canonical inputs are not.
Runtime state is hand-edited and later cited as a reviewed configuration.
Two stores both claim to be the canonical copy of the same record.

hermes_versions.notes: Operational practice control: applies to any deployment layout; the range records the builds whose state layout the classification was read against.

last_verification.notes: General operational synthesis from recorded practice with private detail removed; no specific public incident is claimed.

references: General operational synthesis from recorded practice; no publicly verifiable incident is cited.
